title: Orbital Lounge
premise: A cozy orbital mission-control lounge toy where the player taps space-themed stations to maintain a relaxing shift, raise sync, and enjoy playful audiovisual feedback.
interaction_model: Single-screen tap/click interaction on a full-screen canvas, plus a start button and a separate Flux Mode toggle.
objective: Begin the shift, tap the snack station to raise the Sync score, and casually interact with the TV and phone stations for ambient variation and world flavor.
progression: Progression is light and open-ended: the player starts the session, accumulates score through repeated snack taps, cycles TV channels, triggers floating comms messages, and optionally switches into Flux Mode for an alternate presentation.
theme: Cozy retro-futurist orbital lounge / space station downtime.
mood: Relaxing, playful, neon, soft sci-fi, and lightly whimsical.
likely_audience: players who enjoy cozy low-pressure interactive toys
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a casual one-screen interaction toy built around three tappable zones and a score counter.
Moderate confidence that the intended fantasy is a lounge-shift or mission-control maintenance vignette rather than a goal-driven simulator.
Lower confidence on long-term progression because the code contains no explicit win, loss, stage, or timer system.
recreation_prompt: Create a single-screen browser game called "Orbital Lounge," presented as a cozy neon sci-fi orbital mission-control lounge viewed on a full-screen canvas. The player begins on a polished start overlay, then enters an open-ended shift where a central Earth slowly rotates with a moon and a station orbiting around it against a drifting starfield. Place three large tap targets along the lower portion of the screen: a left-side lounge TV that cycles between different ambient channels like stars, aurora, and static; a center snack bowl filled with colorful cosmic treats that gives the player points whenever tapped; and a right-side phone or comms device that spawns playful floating text messages from planets, spacecraft, or space agencies. Show a minimal HUD with a single score-like stat labeled Sync, and let the snack interaction be the main way to increase it. Add strong tactile feedback for every interaction through particles, sound effects, hit flashes, and brief animated reaction visuals. Include a Flux Mode toggle button in the HUD that transforms the whole presentation into a retro wireframe or debug-style space view with grid lines and simplified neon outlines, while preserving the same core interaction loop. Keep the controls simple and touch-friendly: tap or click the objects on the canvas, use a visible start button to open the shift, and use the Flux button to switch modes. The overall tone should be relaxing, playful, stylish, and low-pressure, with no fail state, no enemies, and no strict ending—just an ambient score-chasing lounge toy with cozy sci-fi presentation, floating comms chatter, and satisfying audiovisual feedback.
